did: I worked the S21 Ultra's Practice banner that kept saying it couldn't find home's name. First I fixed a gap where an answer from home by the live socket or a pairing left the block in place, and took the router guess out of the words. The owner's log then showed the real cause: at home the app's requests went out over mobile data, a carrier's address, while Chrome used Wi-Fi. The app now asks home again over the phone's Wi-Fi when a request never reached it, and logs which network each failure was on. Per the owner's rule I reproduced it first on GitHub's emulators: the S21-like set-up fails without the fix and passes with it, and the S26-like set-up passes both ways, on Android 14 and 16.

calls.title: How the app gets past Android putting its traffic on mobile data
options: ask home over each other local network, and say a held app as held
patch Capacitor's HTTP plugin to take a network
OkHttp with a per-network socket factory
calls.why: Capacitor's HTTP plugin can't take a network, and the other two would add a library or a fork to keep in step for the same Network call. Only Wi-Fi and Ethernet are asked, since home is on the local network, and only after a request that was never sent, so nothing reaches home twice.
calls.undo: Move call C1062: take routeElsewhere out of native-http and HomeRoutePlugin out of MainActivity.

calls.title: Where the S21 reproduction runs and what stands in for each phone
options: a scenario of the existing Android Compat workflow, staged below the app
a new dispatch-only workflow, landed first in its own pull request
the whole app paired with a stand-in home reached by name
calls.why: Android Compat is already on main and runs a branch's own copy when dispatched there, so the reproduction gates the fix before anything merges. API 34 stands in for the S21 Ultra and API 36 for the S26 until the owner gives the exact versions.
